title: APAC Quarterly: Japan's inflation problem
gist: Japanese inflation is re-accelerating on record-high imported goods costs and a structural wage-price spiral (5% average Shunto pay rises for a third year), pushing 10-year JGB yields to a 30-year high of 3% and breaking bonds' diversification role in domestic portfolios. World Gold Council argues gold is the replacement hedge for Japanese investors — 12% annualised over 20 years in yen versus 4% for cash and -1% for holding yen — even though Japanese bar, coin and jewellery demand went negative or fell sharply in Q2 2026 while ETFs absorbed inflows.

insights.claim: Japan's headline CPI rose for three consecutive months through July 2026, and the core-core reading excluding fresh food and energy also bounced, indicating the price pressure is broad rather than confined to volatile components.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: A broadening core print keeps the BoJ tightening bias alive and undermines the case for JGB duration.
insights.quote: Japan’s inflation picked up in July, with the headline print rising three months in a row.
insights.locator: Inflation remains a problem in Japan

insights.claim: The cost of imported goods into Japan reached a record high in July 2026, and Japan's high structural reliance on imported commodities converts that directly into domestic inflationary pressure.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Japanese CPI is now a leveraged bet on global commodity prices and the yen — a weaker yen mechanically imports more inflation.
insights.quote: costs of imported goods have been surging, reaching a record high in July
insights.locator: For one, costs of imported goods have been surging

insights.claim: Commodities including energy and metals may become more expensive on solid global demand and supply disruptions, per the World Bank's April 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook, implying Japan's import-cost channel stays open rather than reversing.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Removes the usual mean-reversion escape valve for Japanese inflation forecasts; favours inflation-linked and real-asset exposure.
insights.locator: And commodities, including energy and metals

insights.claim: Japan's wage-price spiral is framed as a structural rather than cyclical problem, because an ageing population is shrinking the workforce and the Tankan Labour Conditions Index shows persistent labour shortage across large, medium and small companies.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Structural framing means investors should not fade Japanese inflation as a transitory commodity spike; the wage leg persists through cycles.
insights.quote: the intensifying wage-price spiral is keeping Japan’s inflation elevated…and this is a structural issue
insights.locator: Secondly, the intensifying wage-price spiral

insights.claim: Stricter Japanese immigration policy is identified as a constraint on foreign labour supply growth, tightening an already tight domestic labour market rather than relieving it.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Politics, not just demographics, is now an inflation input in Japan — watch immigration policy as a wage-inflation lever.
insights.quote: stricter immigration policies may limit foreign labour supply growth
insights.locator: Furthermore, stricter immigration policies

insights.claim: The 2026 Shunto wage round delivered pay increases averaging 5%, the third consecutive year near multi-decade highs.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Three straight years of 5% pay gains is the hard evidence that Japanese inflation expectations have de-anchored upward; it is the key BoJ input to track each spring.
insights.quote: pay increases averaging 5% in 2026, three consecutive years near multi-decade highs
insights.locator: As a result, labour shortages have supported

themes.theme: BoJ policy and the JGB yield shock

insights.claim: A major driver behind the Bank of Japan's June 2026 rate hike was the upside risk that inflation may deviate upward to a level above its 2% price stability target.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: The BoJ's own stated reaction function is upside-risk driven, so hot prints translate more directly into hikes than in a symmetric-target regime.
insights.quote: …deviate upward to a level above the price stability target of 2%...
insights.locator: What's next: sticky inflation, rising rates

insights.claim: The 10-year JGB yield surged to 3% in early September 2026, the highest level in 30 years, driven by intensifying investor expectations of further BoJ rate hikes.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: A 3% JGB handle repricing global duration and yen-funded carry trades; it is the single most consequential level in the piece.
insights.quote: JGB yields surged to 3% in early September, the highest in 30 years
insights.locator: JGB yields surged to 3% in early September

insights.claim: The Takaichi administration's expansionary fiscal stance, combined with rising social security costs and increased defence spending, is keeping Japanese public debt at record highs and adding a term-premium push to JGB yields on top of the BoJ channel.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Two independent upward forces on JGB yields means a dovish BoJ surprise alone would not cap them; fiscal supply is the second leg.
insights.quote: the Takaichi administration's expansionary fiscal stance, coupled with rising social security costs and increased defence spending, is keeping Japan's public debt at record highs
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the Takaichi administration's expansionary fiscal stance

insights.claim: The upward pressure on Japanese bond yields from fiscal expansion is explicitly expected to persist rather than to be a one-off repricing.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Argues against buying the dip in JGBs on the assumption that 3% is a terminal level.
insights.quote: a trend likely to persist
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the Takaichi administration's expansionary fiscal stance

insights.claim: Rising yields together with higher inflation tend to increase the correlation between bonds and equities, which raises overall portfolio risk rather than dampening it.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: The reusable model here: inflation regime determines whether bonds hedge or amplify equity risk — check the regime before sizing duration.
insights.quote: Rising yields and higher inflation, as we have already analysed, tends to increase the correlation between bonds and equities, raising portfolio risk
insights.locator: Rising yields and higher inflation

insights.claim: On rolling three-year data from January 2006 to August 2026, JGBs' correlation with local equities and their risk contribution to a 40% JGB / 60% TOPIX portfolio show JGBs are currently contributing to, rather than absorbing, portfolio risk.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Japanese 60/40 investors are carrying more risk than their asset weights imply; the diversification budget has to be rebuilt elsewhere.
insights.quote: JGBs not so safe for portfolios right now
insights.locator: Chart 4: JGBs not so safe for portfolios

insights.claim: Potential further BoJ hikes plus rising term premia are presented as jointly lifting JGB yields and therefore increasing portfolio risk for Japanese investors — a risk framed as coming from the bond allocation itself, which is counterintuitive for a market long treated as the definition of safety.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: Reframes the 'safe' leg of Japanese institutional portfolios as the source of risk — a mandate-level rethink, not a tactical trade.
insights.quote: Potential rate hikes from Bank of Japan (BoJ) and rising term premia may continue to lift Japanese Government Bond (JGB) yields, increasing portfolio risks
insights.locator: Summary

insights.claim: Gold rose 7% in yen terms and 4% in USD between January and August 2026, meaning yen-based holders captured roughly three percentage points of extra return from currency effects.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Quantifies the currency kicker in yen-denominated gold — the case for local investors is stronger than the headline dollar chart suggests.
insights.quote: Gold rose 7% in yen terms and 4% in USD between January and August.
insights.locator: Gold's relevance to Japanese investors rising

insights.claim: Short-term US Treasury yields, which depend largely on expectations of future Fed actions, are flagged as the main source of episodic volatility for gold going forward.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Names the specific variable to watch for gold drawdowns: the front end of the US curve, not the long end.
insights.locator: Going forward, short-term US Treasury yields

insights.claim: Mounting concerns over US government debt and intervention by the US Treasury department are cited as supportive factors for gold, positioning US fiscal credibility itself as a gold bid.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: A second-order read: US debt anxiety and gold are becoming the same trade, so US fiscal headlines are gold catalysts.
insights.quote: mounting concerns over US government debt and the Treasury department’s intervention could provide support
insights.locator: But mounting concerns over US government debt

insights.claim: Elevated geopolitical risks and growing portfolio diversification needs are showing up concretely in notable global gold ETF inflows in August 2026 and continued strength in central bank buying.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Two structural bid sources — ETFs and central banks — are confirmed active, which cushions price dips driven by rate expectations.
insights.locator: Elevated geopolitical risks and growing portfolio

insights.claim: Changes in investor positioning, interest rate expectations and dollar strength are identified as the key drivers of gold's 2026 performance, i.e. a financial-flows explanation rather than a physical-demand one.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Consistent with the Japan demand data: gold can rally while physical retail buying falls, so tracking flows beats tracking tonnage.
insights.quote: Changes in investor positioning, interest rate expectations and dollar strength have been key drivers.
insights.locator: Gold's relevance to Japanese investors rising

themes.theme: Gold as inflation hedge and pension diversifier

insights.claim: Over the past 20 years gold delivered a 12% annualised return in yen versus 4% for Japanese cash investments, while simply holding yen lost 1% per year.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: A 800bp annual gap over cash is the headline number to cite when arguing for a gold sleeve in yen-based mandates.
insights.quote: Over the past 20 years gold has delivered a robust annualised return of 12%, compared with 4% for cash investments, while yen holdings lost 1% per year.
insights.locator: Gold as an inflation hedge

insights.claim: After adjusting for Japanese CPI, cash and yen holdings lost most of their purchasing power since January 2006 while gold preserved value and generated attractive real returns — the contrast being starker in real than nominal terms.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Reframes yen cash as a guaranteed real loss, which is the core argument for shifting Japanese household savings out of deposits.
insights.quote: after adjusting for inflation, cash and yen holdings lost most of their purchasing power
insights.locator: The contrast is even starker in real terms

insights.claim: Adding just 5% gold to a typical Japanese corporate pension portfolio reduces overall portfolio volatility and improves returns simultaneously, on monthly JPY data from January 2006 to August 2026.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: A concrete, small allocation size that institutional allocators can propose without restructuring the mandate.
insights.quote: adding just 5% gold reduces overall portfolio volatility and improves returns
insights.locator: Gold to diversify portfolio risks

insights.claim: The benchmark Japanese corporate pension portfolio used in the analysis holds 18.7% Japanese bonds, 17.1% foreign bonds, 9.5% Japanese equities, 13.7% foreign equities, 19.9% alternatives, 16% general account and 5.1% short-term bonds, based on Pension Fund Association data — meaning roughly 41% of assets sit in the bond and general-account buckets now exposed to rising yields.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Shows the size of the Japanese pension pool structurally exposed to the JGB repricing — the potential reallocation flow is large.
insights.locator: *The hypothetical corporate pension portfolio consists

insights.claim: Gold's diversification value is attributed specifically to its low or negative correlation with risk assets, which is the mechanism that lets it substitute for bonds when bond-equity correlation turns positive.
insights.speaker: Ray Jia
insights.so_what: Gives the substitution logic: when the inflation regime breaks bond hedging, rotate the hedge budget to gold rather than abandoning hedging.
insights.locator: Historical records show that gold has enhanced returns

themes.theme: Japanese physical and ETF demand divergence

insights.claim: Japanese consumers bought only 2.2t of gold jewellery in Q2 2026, down 25% year-on-year and 24% quarter-on-quarter, as volatile gold prices deterred buying.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: Price-elastic Asian jewellery demand is capitulating at high prices — a reminder that consumer demand is not what is driving this gold cycle.
insights.quote: Japanese consumers bought 2.2t gold jewellery, 25% down y/y and 24% lower q/q
insights.locator: Gold demand and supply trends in Japan

insights.claim: Japanese net bar and coin investment flipped negative in Q2 2026 to -2.7t, meaning retail investors were net sellers of physical gold.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: Japanese retail is a supply source, not a bid, at current prices — watch for this flipping back as a sentiment signal.
insights.quote: net bar and coin investment flipped negative in the quarter, to -2.7t
insights.locator: Meanwhile, net bar and coin investment flipped

insights.claim: Weakening gold price momentum, surging local bond yields and strong equity performance jointly diverted Japanese investor attention away from gold in Q2 2026.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: Higher domestic yields are a real competing asset for Japanese gold demand — the same 3% JGB that breaks diversification also raises gold's opportunity cost locally.
insights.quote: The weakening gold price momentum, surging local bond yields and strong equity performance all diverted investor attention away from gold.
insights.locator: The weakening gold price momentum

insights.claim: Japanese gold ETF holdings added 5t between January and June 2026 to reach 71.4t, even though bar and coin demand in H1 showed a 0.3t dis-investment and jewellery fell 13% y/y to 5t — a clean split between institutional/ETF buyers and physical retail sellers.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: The Japanese gold bid has shifted channel from physical retail to ETFs; track ETF tonnage, not shop demand, for local sentiment.
insights.quote: Gold ETFs saw healthy inflows, adding 5t to holdings between January and June, and pushing the total to 71.4t.
insights.locator: During the first half of 2026

insights.claim: Japanese gold ETF holdings fell 1t in Q2 2026 and have remained stable so far in Q3, so the H1 inflow was concentrated in Q1 when gold price momentum and geopolitical risk were strongest.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: Japanese ETF demand is momentum-following, so it is a confirming rather than leading indicator for gold.
insights.locator: Local gold ETF holdings were down 1t

insights.claim: Japanese recycled gold supply was 7.6t in Q2 2026 and 15t in H1, slightly lower year-on-year on a lower gold price, but described as staying elevated.
insights.speaker: Marissa Salim
insights.so_what: Elevated recycling plus negative bar and coin demand means Japan is a net physical supplier to the global gold market at these prices.
insights.quote: Recycling pulled back but stayed elevated
insights.locator: Chart 8: Recycling pulled back but stayed elevated
